_comment: Golden set v2 floors (the Phase 14.0 plan, section 14.0 / P14-D4). Recorded by block 14-A2 (T14.0.5). T14.2.8 (block 14-C2) turns enforcement on PER METRIC (the `enforce` object below) instead of 14-A2's single global `enforce_now` switch: a metric is enforced once its floor is both in force (14.2 onward, i.e. every floor here) and actually met by the measured numbers; `enforce_now` is kept only as a human-readable note of when enforcement as a concept started, no longer read by gate.py.
_enforce_comment: block 14-C2 (T14.2.8): noisy_recall (1.000), greeting_reply_p95_s (~1.48s) and router_p95_s (~1.05s local) enforced from that block. Block 14-C3 (T14.2.9, DEC-062) adds follow_up_resolution: measured 0.900 on BOTH final verification runs (gate-20261125T130554Z-2888977.log and gate-20261125T131222Z-2925883.log, --only eval, n=10 follow-up turns after this block's +4 dialogues) -- clears the 0.85 floor reliably, not a one-off, so enforced from this block on. 14-C3 also left intent_accuracy at 0.840 (below its 0.90 floor, DOWN from 14-C2's 0.873 on the smaller 63-turn fixture) -- a router ambiguous-vs-followup boundary confusion on terse, several-turns-back follow-ups (DEC-063). Block 14-C4 (T14.2.9-fix, DEC-063 = B) fixes it: one more contrasting few-shot plus a deterministic, code-level tie-breaker (`router._resolves_a_reference`) that corrects an 'ambiguous' verdict to 'followup' whenever conversation context existed AND the model's own standalone_query already resolved the reference from it (live-verified against the real router on both DA-14-C3 regression cases before the gate runs below). Measured 0.907 on BOTH final `--only eval` runs (gate-20261125T180052Z-3120649.log and gate-20261125T180723Z-3121974.log, n=75) -- clears the 0.90 floor reliably on both, so `intent_accuracy` is enforced from this block on. `conversational_reply_rate` also measured 1.000 on both of the SAME two runs (up from 14-C3's 0.944) but was left `false` there: 14-C4's scope was intent_accuracy + follow_up_resolution only. Block eval-determinism (DEC-064) proved the TRUE deterministic baseline (seed 42, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1) was actually intent_accuracy 0.867 and follow_up_resolution 0.700-0.800 -- both below their floors -- and conversational_reply_rate 0.833-0.889, never 1.0, on 4/4 deterministic measurements (the earlier 'passing' numbers were non-deterministic excursions above the real, reproducible value). Block router-reliability (DEC-066) fixes all three with 5 deterministic changes (see `docs/adr/adr_phase14_assistant.md`'s own section): measured on 2 real `--only eval` runs on the FINAL code, BYTE-IDENTICAL -- intent_accuracy 0.9733333333333334, follow_up_resolution 1.0, noisy_recall 1.0, conversational_reply_rate 1.0, both runs (gate-20261126T003647Z-3588786.log, gate-20261126T004905Z-3590916.log) -- clears every floor with a large margin on both, so `conversational_reply_rate` is enforced from this block on too, per the orchestrator's own rule ('enforce if 1.0 in both runs'). Flipping a floor's `enforce` to `true` without first raising the real number would fail `gate.sh --full` outright; the two byte-identical runs above prove every floor is genuinely met, not a one-off.
